answer.rationale: Primary expires in 14 days with no auto-renewal, so deferring or only adding a second source leaves a supply cliff on a line at 94% with no buffer. Incumbent has already refused to reopen price, so renew/negotiate cannot meet the mandated 18% spend cut. The low-cost quote is the only path that hits the cost target and replaces the expiring primary. That intent rests on unverified consolidated notes: c2 (prior low-cost primary move was quick and clean) and c1 (incumbent renewal avoided migration risk). Those two archives must be checked before treating switch risk as low. Scale is a standard experiment, not a broad rollout, because disruption would dominate TCO. Downstream assembly-line risk is flagged; onboarding speed and true switching cost remain uncertain.
